title: Probabilistic slab leasing and micro-defrag TTL for KV cache to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Long-lived, partially filled KV cache slabs and deterministic eviction policies cause fragmentation hotspots on GPU memory which degrade throughput for continuous batching workloads. Current approaches (coarse compaction sweeps or aggressive whole-slab reclamation) either spike latency or waste compute/GPU cycles.

Proposal: Implement a probabilistic slab leasing mechanism combined with a micro-defrag TTL trigger. Slab leasing performs lightweight probabilistic reassignments of underutilized slab segments to active token streams; leases are short-lived and amortized across requests. The micro-defrag TTL marks slabs that have below-threshold utilization for a time window and schedules small background relocations constrained by a per-GPU IOP/latency budget. Together the leasing plus TTL-based micro-defrag reduces long-tail fragmentation while avoiding large synchronous compaction jobs.

Goals: Reduce measurable fragmentation metric (free contiguous region size) by >= 40% on average for mixed-length workloads; keep p95 token latency regression < 5%; limit background GPU time for defrag to < 2% on steady-state.

Scope: Runtime allocator and KV cache controller changes; add telemetry; runtime config flags; gradual rollout via canary on dedicated pools and then to hosted clusters. No model format changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Probabilistic slab leasing mechanism implemented behind feature flag and configurable lease probability/period.
A2: Micro-defrag TTL implemented with adjustable thresholds (utilization, idle_time) and per-GPU background budget enforcement.
A3: End-to-end tests that exercise leasing + micro-defrag under small/medium/large sequence workloads with continuous batching enabled.
A4: Telemetry dashboards showing fragmentation heatmap, background defrag CPU/GPU usage, lease churn rate, and token latency percentiles.
A5: Canary rollout on 10% of Dedicated pools with rollback plan and no more than 5% regression in tail latency observed during canary.
A6: Documentation and runtime knobs added to runtime-1.19 release notes.
A7: Security review: ensure lease metadata cannot be used to leak request correlation information (privacy check completed).
implementation_notes: Design leasing as a probabilistic sampler on eviction/hint paths: when slab usage < low_watermark, with probability p reassign a small segment (1-4 pages) to a lease token which pins it for lease_duration_ms unless actively touched.
Leases are soft: they can be preempted by high-priority allocations if needed to meet latency SLOs. Preemptions increment a lease-preempt counter for telemetry.
Micro-defrag TTL: track per-slab last_active_ts and tracked_util_pct. If tracked_util_pct < threshold for ttl_ms, schedule a micro-relocate job capped by gpu_defrag_budget_ms_per_minute.
Micro-relocate operates on page-granularity and favors relocating hot KV entries out of interleaved cold slots rather than moving data out of active chunks synchronously.
Allocator changes localized to gpu_kv_allocator module with feature-flag toggle and runtime-config via console/remote-config.
Add counters and histograms: slab_free_runs_size, lease_attempts, lease_successes, lease_preempts, micro_reloc_jobs, micro_reloc_latency_ms, defrag_gpu_busy_ms.
Ensure continuous-batching integration: leasing should be a no-op on short-living inference streams (seq_len < sampling_min_len) to avoid thrashing.
Failure modes: if micro-defrag queue backs up, throttle new defrag jobs and raise alert; provide auto-disable if p95 latency rises above safe threshold.
telemetry: Dashboard: KV Fragmentation — heatmap of contiguous free region sizes by GPU and slab-class.
Alert: micro_defrag_backpressure (> 80% budget sustained for 3 minutes) -> Paging on-call infra team.
Logging: sample relocation operations with before/after slab map for offline analysis (rate-limited).
rollout_plan: Step 1: Unit + integration tests, run allocator simulator on synthetic traces (2 days).
Step 2: Internal staging deploy with debug telemetry (3 days).
Step 3: Canary: enable on 10% of Dedicated pools for 1 week, monitor fragmentation and latency.
Step 4: Expand to 50% if safe, run 48-hour soak test under mixed workloads.
Step 5: Gradual global rollout to hosted clusters with optional auto-disable if errors or tail latency regression detected.
Rollback: flip runtime flag off and trigger immediate defrag backfill disable; automation to drain micro-reloc queue gracefully.
risks: Risk: Leasing could introduce extra metadata churn and increase allocator lock contention if not implemented lock-free; mitigate by sharding slab maps per-CPU and using CAS-based updates.
Risk: Background micro-relocations could consume GPU cycles and increase p95; mitigation: strict budget enforcement and early auto-disable on regression.
Risk: Incorrect heuristics may cause oscillation (repeated lease->preempt cycles). Mitigate by adding exponential backoff on preempted slabs and hysteresis in TTL thresholds.
Risk: Telemetry volume increase; ensure sampling and aggregation to avoid OOM on metrics collector.
